extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and legal counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) based on a state court disbarment and setting forth procedural requirements, notices, and post-discipline obligations for a registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 / §10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO is ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5), predicated upon being excluded from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed identical to the discipline imposed by the State (here, disbarment by the Supreme Court of the State of Delaware). The Order expressly cites the predicate state exclusion as the basis for USPTO exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (37 C.F.R. §11.24 procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24 must be mailed (here by certified mail) to the respondent and must provide an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline under the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice/Order was mailed to business and personal addresses; delivery dates and certified-mail receipts are recorded. The availability of a 40-day response period to raise statutory defenses under §11.24(d)(1) is a critical procedural safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and find reciprocal discipline appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, Respondent's failure to respond led to the determination that exclusion was appropriate. The Order makes clear that non-response may result in imposition of identical discipline without further contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of discipline in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the exact form of a Notice of Exclusion summarizing charges, rules violated, and that action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24; disciplinary notices are posted in OED's Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation ensures dissemination of disciplinary information to relevant state and federal entities as well as the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. §11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not restate §11.58, it imposes the practitioner's regulatory duties (e.g., notification/ reporting obligations) that accompany public discipline and exclusion; practitioners must consult §11.58 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the disciplined practitioner's continued use of USPTO electronic access tied to those identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative bar on electronic filing/representation through USPTO systems until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action (35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders must be grounded in statutory and regulatory authority; practitioners and decisionmakers should cite applicable statutes/regulations when imposing or reviewing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged misconduct categories relied on by state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Delaware disciplinary complaint alleged violations of Delaware Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.15(a), 1.15(d)(9)(c), 3.4(c), 8.1(d), 8.4(c), and 8.4(d). Allegations included submitting false annual Certificates of Compliance regarding books and records, failing to maintain continuing legal education requirements, failing to have safeguarded client funds, and repeatedly failing to respond to requests from the Office of Disciplinary Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These types of lawyer misconduct (false statements to a court/authority, CLE noncompliance, mishandling client funds, and non-cooperation with disciplinary investigations) are recognized bases for state discipline and thus can serve as predicates for USPTO reciprocal discipline under §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial and ancillary relief (scope of order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order may include additional relief 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary orders can combine exclusion with ancillary measures (notice, dissociation from systems, compliance requirements) and retain flexibility to order further relief as necessary.
